A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Freeze-Omni and provide readable text, figures and tables supporting a complete comparison. All 11 pages of each were inspected; both end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Freeze-Omni ASR, speech-generation, spoken-question-answering and latency results in Tables 1–4, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds speech-generation results for pre-network variants in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces an evaluated variant with a two-layer Llama pre-network between the LLM embedding layer and NAR speech decoder. This adds dedicated processing capacity while retaining the frozen backbone and three-stage training design. Revised interruption wording does not establish a different state-prediction algorithm.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: Chinese/English ASR, single-speaker speech generation, the same three spoken-QA benchmarks, and latency evaluation. The added pre-network variants and comparator introduce no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GLM-4-Voice (9B) to the spoken-QA comparison, using results attributed to its reference. Existing QA comparators and the Wav2vec2-base/Mini-Omni2 ASR comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Table 2 extends the experimental controls by evaluating the additional pre-network both with and without prefix conditioning. The 1,000-utterance single-speaker evaluation, CER metric and top-k sweep remain unchanged. Removed hardware specifications do not establish an actual hardware change.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 and Table 2 add an ablation testing whether dedicated processing of LLM embeddings improves synthesis, across both prefix configurations and five top-k values. Existing prefix, chunk-size and dynamic-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean, median and 90th-percentile latency. Neither provides repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added results do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds pre-network results: at top-k=2, CER is 2.75% without prefix and 1.69% with prefix, versus retained original-configuration values of 4.64% and 3.65%. Table 3 adds GLM-4-Voice accuracies of 32.2%, 64.7% and 39.1%. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The pre-network rationale is conceptual, and revised operational descriptions do not introduce mathematical derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the small-training-data contribution to paired Q&A data and reframes duplex interaction from the LLM interrupting or rejecting users to detecting user interruption. The central frozen-LLM, retained-intelligence and low-latency claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a mechanism explanation: LLM embeddings and speech tokens occupy different representation spaces, motivating dedicated pre-network parameters. Section 2.4 also revises the interpretation of interruption states. Existing applicability boundaries and future-work limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 specifies the added pre-network's two Llama decoder layers. However, Section 3.1.3 removes NVIDIA A100 from the eight-GPU training disclosure, and Table 4 removes the single-A100 inference specification, reducing reproducibility information for the unchanged latency results.

R1.justification: v5 adds Zeng et al., Scaling speech-text pre-training with synthetic interleaved data, as the reference supporting GLM-4-Voice's Table 3 results. Other cited works and the positioning around frozen-backbone speech alignment remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and future-work bullets receive language revisions, interruption terminology is adjusted, and Yunhang Shen is added to the author list. Section ordering and most method and experimental prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 gain rows, Table 1 moves from page 7 to 8, and Table 3 moves from page 8 to 9. Figure 3 corrects Refix to Prefix. The overall visual structure is retained, but Table 3's caption still says four speech-input rows although v5 contains five.

improvement.justification: The added pre-network ablation provides useful evidence about speech-decoder design, and GLM-4-Voice broadens the relevant QA comparison. These modest empirical benefits are tempered by removal of hardware details needed to interpret latency and the stale Table 3 caption. The original central QA and latency evidence is unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
